diffs.diff: pin count: part has 5 (GND 3V3 SDA SCL VIN), datasheet reading has 4 (GND 3V3 SDA SCL)
diffs.evidence: The second reading counted only the 4-pin logic header; the model's fifth pin VIN is the board's separate relay-power input (barrel jack), which SparkFun documents as required for the relays: 'There are two separate power systems on the Quad Relay: a 5V system that powers the relays and a 3.3V system' and 'The on board barrel jack takes a power source in a range of 7-12V', so GND/3V3/SDA/SCL match and VIN (7-12 V) is a real, necessary input rather than an extra header pin.

diffs.diff: minimum supply: part 3 V, datasheet reading 3.3 V
diffs.evidence: 3.3 V is the nominal logic rail ('a 3.3V system that powers the on board ATtiny84A'), not a minimum; the 3V3 pin feeds the ATtiny84A, whose datasheet allows '0 – 10 MHz @ 2.7 – 5.5V' and the firmware runs it at 8 MHz ('ATtiny84 needs to run at 8MHz'), so 3.0 V is a conservative minimum above the chip's real 2.7 V limit.

diffs.diff: maximum supply: part 3.6 V, datasheet reading 3.3 V
diffs.evidence: SparkFun gives only the nominal 3.3 V logic rail ('To provide 3.3V to the on board ATtiny84A you can use the plated through hole labeled 3V3'), and the ATtiny84A itself tolerates '0 – 10 MHz @ 2.7 – 5.5V', so 3.6 V is a conservative +10% ceiling on a 3.3 V rail, far below the chip limit.
